document.title: Why durable queues matter
document.summary: A visual explanation of how durable execution turns fragile multi-step work into an observable, resumable process.

blocks.title: The mental model
blocks.html:
A request that spans several services is not one action. It is a sequence of commitments, each with its own failure boundary. A durable queue records those commitments so the system can continue after a worker exits, a network call times out, or a deploy interrupts execution.

The queue does not remove failure. It makes failure visible and recoverable.

blocks.title: Core principle
blocks.text: If work matters after the current process disappears, its state must live somewhere more durable than memory.

blocks.title: An idempotent handler
A common mistake
blocks.html: Retries are not automatically safe. A retried handler can charge a card, send a message, or create a record twice unless the side effect has an idempotency boundary.

blocks.title: Recovery layers
blocks.html:
Record intent

Persist what should happen and assign a stable identity.

Observe attempts

Track start, heartbeat, result, and terminal error.

Resume safely

Retry from durable state with idempotent side effects.
